title: Man. Post. Cap. X tip — if no law required that imputation, how is punishing it judicial?
pass_a_gloss: If it is not by any law, how is it a judicial act, and how is that imputed sin punished so as to satisfy law and justice? For no law required that it be so imputed, and the imputed sin so punished.
pass_b_english: If it does not take place according to some law, how is it a judicial act, and how is that imputed sin so punished that law and justice are satisfied?
For no law required that it be so imputed, and that the imputed sin be punished.
source_text: Si non fiat secundum aliquam legem, quomodo est actio iudiciaria, & punitur sic imputatum illud peccatum, ut legi & iustitiae satisfiat? Nulla enim lex ut sic imputaretur, & imputatum puniretur, exigebat.

choices.choice: Without a law, imputed-act punishment is not judicial

notes: Cap. X reatus densify section 694 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 365–367 tip).
